definition_zh: 治疗；疗法；对待；处理；处理方式
definition_en: the care given to cure an illness or injury, or the way a person or thing is dealt with
core_image: 病床边挂着输液袋，护士按表一格一格记录换药
scene: 住院部的床头挂着卡片，护士按上面的疗程逐日换药记录。The new treatment reduced the pain within a week.
sceneCN: 这里 treatment 是「治疗、疗法」（第 1 个义项：为治愈而给的医疗照护）；句意为新疗法一周内就减轻了疼痛。床头那张逐日记录的卡片正是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 去掉后缀 -ment 还原为动词，义为「对待；治疗」
由 treat 加 -able 构成，义为「可治疗的」
加前缀 mis- 构成，义为「虐待」

senses.title: Medical care for an illness
senses.definition: the care and medicine given to cure a disease or injury
senses.definitionCN: 为治愈疾病或伤处而给的照护与药物
senses.example: She is receiving treatment for the infection.
senses.exampleCN: 她正在接受感染治疗。
senses.why: Treating a patient is handling the body back to health, and the noun names that handling.
senses.whyCN: 治疗病人就是把身体料理回健康，名词指的就是这份料理。

senses.title: A particular method of healing
senses.definition: a specific way of treating a disease
senses.definitionCN: 治疗某种病的具体办法
senses.example: The clinic offers two treatments for the knee.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所对膝关节有两种疗法。
senses.why: Once methods are compared, the noun shifts from care in general to one named method.
senses.whyCN: 一旦比较各种方法，名词就从笼统的照护转向某一种有名字的疗法。

senses.title: The way a person is dealt with
senses.definition: the way someone is behaved towards
senses.definitionCN: 别人对待某人的方式
senses.example: The workers asked for fair treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们要求公平对待。
senses.why: The oldest sense of treat is to behave towards, so treatment is simply how that behaves out.
senses.whyCN: treat 最老的含义就是「朝向某人的行为」，treatment 就是把这种行为表现出的样子。

senses.title: A process applied to a material
senses.definition: a process that is applied to a substance to change it
senses.definitionCN: 为使物质改变而施加的工序
senses.example: The water needs chemical treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 这水需要化学处理。
senses.why: Handling a material is the same handling as handling a person, only without feeling.
senses.whyCN: 处理材料与待人同属「处理」，只是对象没有感情。

senses.title: A way of presenting a subject
senses.definition: the way a writer or artist deals with a subject
senses.definitionCN: 作者或艺术家处理题材的方式
senses.example: Her treatment of the war is very restrained.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这场战争的处理很克制。
senses.why: Tractare also meant to discuss, so how a subject is discussed is its treatment.
senses.whyCN: tractare 也有讨论义，所以一个题目被怎样讨论，就是它的「处理方式」。

intro.en: The noun is treat plus -ment, and treat comes from Latin tractare, to handle.
intro.cn: 这个名词是 treat 加 -ment，而 treat 出自拉丁语 tractare（处理）。

items.en: Tractare is the frequentative of trahere, to draw, and means to keep handling.
items.cn: tractare 是 trahere（拉）的反复形式，意为反复摆弄。

items.en: Traitier gives the English verb treat, for dealing with people and matters.
items.cn: 古法语 traitier 生出英语动词 treat，用于待人与处事。

items.en: The -ment ending turns the verb into a noun of the handling itself.
items.cn: -ment 词尾把动词变成表示「处理本身」的名词。

items.en: Medicine makes the medical sense the dominant one in modern use.
items.cn: 现代用法中，医学义成了最主要的义项。

items.en: Industry and journalism extend it to water, waste, and the handling of subjects.
items.cn: 工业与新闻业把它扩展到水、废物与题材的处理上。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the treat- stem, while the near-meaning group gathers other words for care and handling.
note.cn: 形近组共用 treat- 词干，近义组汇集表示照护与处理的其他说法。

a formal written agreement
a long written work
cruel or unfair handling
treatment to cure a condition
medicine used to treat illness
a treatment that makes someone well
the way something is dealt with

normalIntro.en: Treat plus -ment: the verb known, the noun follows.
normalIntro.cn: 在 treat 后加上 -ment，动词认识了，名词就跟着来。

normal.en: Treat is to handle, and -ment makes that handling into a thing.
normal.cn: treat 是处理，-ment 把这份处理变成一样东西。

normal.en: Treatment in a hospital is handling a body back to health.
normal.cn: 医院里的 treatment 是把身体料理回健康。

normal.en: Mistreatment adds mis-, meaning handling the wrong way.
normal.cn: mistreatment 加 mis-，意为用错方式对待。

normal.en: Water treatment plants handle water, not patients.
normal.cn: 水处理厂处理的是水，不是病人。

normal.en: The word appears in headlines about fair and unfair handling alike.
normal.cn: 这个词既见于公平对待的标题，也见于不公对待的标题。

abstract.en: Picture a card at the head of a hospital bed, ticked each day.
abstract.cn: 想象床头一张卡片，每天打一个勾。

abstract.en: Hear the drip counted in drops.
abstract.cn: 听输液一滴一滴地数。

abstract.en: Then move the same careful tick to a water tank and to a worker’s pay.
abstract.cn: 再把同样的仔细勾画挪到水池与工人的工资上。

examples.en: He began treatment for the disease last spring.
examples.cn: 他去年春天开始接受该病的治疗。

examples.en: The staff received training in the fair treatment of patients.
examples.cn: 员工接受了公平对待病人的培训。

examples.en: The plant provides treatment for waste water.
examples.cn: 这座工厂负责废水的处理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吹特门」——吹一口气特别把门关好，小心护理，这就是治疗。

root: 拉丁语 tractare（处理）+ 后缀 -ment，由动词 treat 构成；同族有 treat、treaty、treatise、mistreatment

sensesIntro.en: The word covers handling of every kind, with healing as the most familiar branch.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词涵盖各种各样的「处理」，其中以治疗最为人熟悉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a card at a hospital bed, ticked once each day.
core.cn: 核心意象：床头一张卡片，每天打一个勾。

branches.en: The healing sense, first as care, then as a named method.
branches.cn: 治疗义：先是照护，再是具体的疗法。

branches.en: The fairness sense, how people behave towards people.
branches.cn: 公平义：人与人之间怎样相待。

branches.en: The industrial sense, where a material is the patient.
branches.cn: 工业义：被处理的是材料。

branches.en: The artistic sense, how a subject is presented.
branches.cn: 艺术义：一个题材被怎样呈现。

branches.en: The method sense, where a named cure is chosen.
branches.cn: 方法义：选出一种有名字的治法。

intro.en: The noun adds a Latin suffix to a French verb of handling.
intro.cn: 这个名词给一个法语「处理」动词加上拉丁名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The tract- stem runs through treat, treatment, treaty, contract, and extract.
latinIntro.cn: tract- 词干贯穿 treat、treatment、treaty、contract 与 extract。

items.example: The stem gives contract and extract.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干生出 contract 与 extract。

items.example: They treat the staff well.
Treat gives treatment.
The treatment worked quickly.
The disease is treatable.
Mis- plus treat gives mistreat.
items.exampleCN: mis- 加 treat 成为 mistreat。

items.example: The case involved mistreatment.

items.meaning: the way something is dealt with
items.example: Careful handling saves the crop.
Speech therapy helps children.
items.exampleCN: 言语治疗对孩子有帮助。

definition_zh: 条约；协议；协定
definition_en: a formal written agreement between two or more countries, signed by their governments
core_image: 长桌两端两位代表同时落笔，纸页上并排着两种文字的签名
scene: 大厅里两张长桌拼在一起，两国的代表各自翻开文件夹。The two countries signed a peace treaty after a year of talks.
sceneCN: 这里 treaty 是「条约」（第 1 个义项：两国或多国政府签署的正式书面协议）；句意为经过一年谈判，两国签署了和平条约。长桌上并排的两份签名，就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: treaty 的词源动词，义为「对待；谈判」
由 treat 加 -ment 构成，义为「对待；处理」
与 treaty 同源的词，义为「论文；专著」

senses.title: The signed paper
senses.definition: a formal agreement between states, written down and signed by those in power
senses.definitionCN: 国家之间写下并由掌权者签署的正式协议
senses.example: The two countries signed a peace treaty after a year of talks.
senses.exampleCN: 经过一年谈判，两国签署了和平条约。
senses.why: Medieval Latin tractatus meant a handling or a discussion, and a treaty is the paper produced when talks end.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪拉丁语 tractatus 意为处理或讨论，treaty 就是讨论结束后产生的那份文书。

senses.title: A deal between groups
senses.definition: an agreement of the same kind made by other large bodies such as companies
senses.definitionCN: 公司等大型机构之间订立的同类协议
senses.example: The two firms signed a treaty on sharing the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司就共用港口签署了一份协议。
senses.why: The word began to travel from governments to any body large enough to act like one.
senses.whyCN: 这个词开始从政府延伸到任何大到能像政府一样行动的机构。

intro.en: Treaty comes from the Latin verb tractare, to handle or discuss, through the noun tractatus, a discussion.
intro.cn: treaty 经由名词 tractatus（讨论）来自拉丁语动词 tractare（处理、商谈）。

items.en: Tractare meant to drag, handle, and later to discuss or negotiate.
items.cn: tractare 意为拖动、处理，后来指讨论与商谈。

items.en: Tractatus named a treatment or a written discussion of a subject.
items.cn: tractatus 指一次处理，或对某主题的书面论述。

items.en: French made traitie, a discussion that ends in an agreement.
items.cn: 法语造出 traitie，指以协议告终的商讨。

items.en: English treaty first meant any negotiation between rulers.
items.cn: 中古英语的 treaty 最初指统治者之间的任何谈判。

items.en: By the modern period the word meant the signed document itself.
items.cn: 到了近代，这个词指已签署的文件本身。

note.en: The first group shares the tract stem, the second holds other words for formal agreements.
note.cn: 第一组共享 tract 词干，第二组收其他表示正式协定的词。

entries.definition: To behave toward someone or to give medical care.
The way a person or thing is handled.
A long written work on a subject.
An arrangement accepted by both sides.
A firm promise between parties.
A formal settlement between states.

normalIntro.en: Treaty hides the same root as treat: talks that end in a treaty are talks that have been handled to a finish.
normalIntro.cn: treaty 藏着与 treat 相同的词根：以条约结束的谈判，就是把事情处理到底的商谈。

normal.en: The plural changes y to ies: treaties.
normal.cn: 复数把 y 变 ies：treaties。

normal.en: The word begins with treat, the everyday verb.
normal.cn: 这个词以日常动词 treat 开头。

normal.en: A peace treaty is the most common phrase of all.
normal.cn: peace treaty 是最常见的搭配。

normal.en: The stress is on the first syllable: TREAty.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：TREAty。

normal.en: A treaty is signed, broken, or kept, like a promise on paper.
normal.cn: 条约和纸上的承诺一样，会被签署、违反或遵守。

abstract.en: Two pens meeting on the same line.
abstract.cn: 两支笔落在同一条线上。

abstract.en: A page with two languages and two seals.
abstract.cn: 一张写着两种语言、盖着两枚印章的纸。

abstract.en: The silence after the last signature.
abstract.cn: 最后一个签名之后的那份安静。

examples.en: Both sides hope to reach a treaty before the winter.
examples.cn: 双方希望在入冬前达成一项条约。

examples.en: The old treaty fixed the border along the river.
examples.cn: 旧条约以河流划定边界。

examples.en: They met to discuss a trade agreement between the neighbours.
examples.cn: 他们开会讨论邻国之间的贸易协定。

dict_mnemonic.text: treat（商谈处理）＋ y——商谈到底后签下的那张纸，就是条约。

root: 经由古法语 traitie 来自拉丁语 tractatus（处理、讨论），词根 tract- 意为「拉、处理」；同源词有 treat、treatment、treatise。

sensesIntro.en: First the signed document between states, then the same kind of deal between large bodies.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是国家之间签署的文件，再是大型机构之间的同类协议。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two pens landing on the same line.
core.cn: 核心意象：两支笔落在同一行上。

branches.en: The state branch: an agreement between governments.
branches.cn: 国家分支：政府之间的协议。

branches.en: The body branch: a deal between large groups.
branches.cn: 机构分支：大集团之间的协议。

branches.en: The paper branch: both end in a signed document.
branches.cn: 文书分支：两者都以签署的文件告终。

branches.en: The border branch: treaties draw lines on maps.
branches.cn: 边界分支：条约在地图上画线。

branches.en: The talk branch: all of it begins as discussion.
branches.cn: 商谈分支：一切从讨论开始。

intro.en: Treaty is built on the Latin stem tract, drawn or handled, with an Old French noun ending on top.
intro.cn: treaty 建在拉丁词干 tract（拉、处理）之上，外面套着古法语的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin trahere, to pull, gives the family of tract, treat, and treaty, listed below.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 trahere（拉）生出 tract、treat 与 treaty 这一词族，列在下面。

items.example: The root links pulling and dealing with people.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根把「拉」与「应对人」连在一起。

items.example: It turns the handling into a document.
items.exampleCN: 它把处理的过程变成一份文件。

items.meaning: to behave toward, to deal with
items.example: The verb keeps the plain sense of handling.
items.exampleCN: 动词保留处理的朴素含义。

items.example: The noun names the finished paper.
Ment marks the manner of handling.
A treatise handles a subject on paper.
items.exampleCN: treatise 在纸上处理一个主题。

items.example: Here the root pulls in a literal sense.
items.exampleCN: 这里词根是字面意义上的拉。

items.example: Ad means toward, so things are pulled near.
items.exampleCN: ad 意为朝向，于是把东西拉近。

definition_zh: 树；树木；树状图
definition_en: a tall plant with a wooden trunk and branches, or a branching diagram
core_image: 一棵大树在空地上撑开满枝的绿，树影铺过整条路
scene: 村口的空地上站着一棵老树，枝叶向四面伸展。An old tree at the village gate shades the whole road.
sceneCN: 这里 tree 是「树；树木」（第 1 个义项：有木质树干和枝条的高大植物）；句意为村口一棵老树把整条路都遮在荫里。空地上撑开枝叶的那棵老树，就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 由 tree 加 -less 构成，义为「没有树的；无树木的」
由 tree 与 lined 复合，义为「两旁有树的」
由 tree 与 top 复合，义为「树梢」

senses.title: The tall plant
senses.definition: a plant with a hard wooden stem that grows tall and lives for many years
senses.definitionCN: 有坚硬木质主干、长得高大且寿命多年的植物
senses.example: An old tree at the village gate shades the whole road.
senses.exampleCN: 村口一棵老树把整条路都遮在荫里。
senses.why: The word has stayed close to its old English shape for more than a thousand years, naming the same thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词一千多年来与它古英语的形态几乎不变，指的一直是同一件事。

senses.title: The branching drawing
senses.definition: a diagram whose lines branch out like the limbs of a tree
senses.definitionCN: 线条像树枝一样分岔的图表
senses.example: She drew the family tree on the back of an envelope.
senses.exampleCN: 她在信封背面画出了家谱。
senses.why: Because a trunk divides into branches, any chart that divides in this way borrows the word.
senses.whyCN: 因为树干分叉成枝，任何按这种方式分岔的图表都借用了这个词。

senses.title: Planting a memory
senses.definition: a tree planted to mark a person, an event, or a promise for the future
senses.definitionCN: 为纪念某人、某事或对未来的承诺而种下的树
senses.example: They planted a tree at the gate when their daughter was born.
senses.exampleCN: 女儿出生时，他们在门口种了一棵树。
senses.why: A tree outlives the person who plants it, so it became a living record, and the word carries that hope.
senses.whyCN: 树比种它的人活得更久，于是它成了一份活着的记录，这个词也带上了这种期望。

intro.en: Tree is one of the oldest words in English, unchanged in meaning since the Germanic period.
intro.cn: tree 是英语中最古老的词之一，自日耳曼语时期起词义未曾改变。

items.en: The Germanic root trewam named wood, tree, and the material of timber.
items.cn: 日耳曼语词根 trewam 指树、木以及木材。

items.en: Old English treow meant both a tree and the idea of faithfulness, a pair still visible in true.
items.cn: 古英语 treow 既指树，也指忠信，这一双义仍留在 true 里。

items.en: Middle English tre kept the plant sense and dropped the abstract one.
items.cn: 中古英语 tre 保留了植物的意义，舍弃了抽象义。

items.en: The spelling tree settled in the modern period.
items.cn: tree 这个拼写在近代固定下来。

items.en: Compounds such as treetop and tree-lined later built a whole family around it.
items.cn: treetop 与 tree-lined 等复合词后来围绕它建起整个词族。

note.en: The first group collects woody plants, the second collects branching or related forms.
note.cn: 第一组是木本植物，第二组是带枝干意象的词与相关形式。

entries.definition: The highest part of a tree.
Having no trees.
Having trees along its sides.
A low woody plant with many stems.
A small woody plant, smaller than a tree.
Wood prepared for building.

normalIntro.en: Tree is short and long-lived, a word whose sound has barely moved in a thousand years.
normalIntro.cn: tree 短小而长久，这个词的读音一千年几乎没变。

normal.en: The ending ee is long, like the vowel in see.
normal.cn: 词尾 ee 读长音，像 see 里的元音。

normal.en: A family tree draws people as branches.
normal.cn: 家谱把人画成枝条。

normal.en: The plural simply adds s: trees.
normal.cn: 复数只加 s：trees。

normal.en: Treetop and treeline both put the tree first.
normal.cn: treetop 与 treeline 都把 tree 放在前面。

normal.en: The old meaning of faithfulness survives in the word true.
normal.cn: 忠信的古义留在 true 这个词里。

abstract.en: A trunk going up and then becoming many things.
abstract.cn: 一根树干向上走，然后变成许多东西。

abstract.en: Shade moving slowly across a road.
abstract.cn: 荫影缓慢地爬过一条路。

abstract.en: Roots as thick below as branches above.
abstract.cn: 地下的根和上面的枝一样粗。

examples.en: Two children are climbing the tree by the wall.
examples.cn: 两个孩子正在爬墙边的树。

examples.en: The branches of the apple tree touched the roof.
examples.cn: 苹果树的枝条碰到了屋顶。

examples.en: He traced the family branches back four hundred years.
examples.cn: 他把这支家谱追到了四百年前。

dict_mnemonic.text: tree 读音像「吹」——风一吹，满树的叶子都在动。

root: 古英语 treow，来自日耳曼语词根 trewam（木、树），与 true 的「忠信」古义同源；同族词有 treetop、treeless、tree-lined。

sensesIntro.en: First the living plant, then any diagram whose parts branch the way a tree does.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是活着的植物，再是任何像树一样分岔的图表。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a broad old tree shading a road.
core.cn: 核心意象：遮住一条路的老树。

branches.en: The plant branch: root, trunk, and leaf.
branches.cn: 植物分支：根、干与叶。

branches.en: The chart branch: lines that divide like limbs.
branches.cn: 图表分支：像枝干一样分开的线。

branches.en: The shape branch: both share one silhouette.
branches.cn: 形状分支：两者共有一个轮廓。

branches.en: The shade branch: a living tree changes the street.
branches.cn: 荫影分支：活树改变了街道。

branches.en: The family branch: names placed on the limbs.
branches.cn: 家族分支：名字被放到枝条上。

intro.en: Tree is a free Germanic stem that joins freely with other words to make compounds.
intro.cn: tree 是日耳曼语系的自由词干，可以自由与其他词组合成复合词。

latinIntro.en: The tree word itself is Germanic, but Latin supplies the woodland words below.
latinIntro.cn: 树这个词本身来自日耳曼语，但下面的林地词汇出自拉丁语。

items.example: The stem stands on its own as a full noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干本身就是一个完整名词。

items.example: It forms treeless, without any trees.
It forms treetop, the crown of a tree.
It forms tree-lined, with trees along the street.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 tree-lined，街道两旁有树。

items.example: Trees were planted along the river.

items.meaning: a shelter built in a tree
items.example: The children built a treehouse in summer.
items.exampleCN: 孩子们夏天搭了一座树屋。

items.meaning: the height above which trees cannot grow
items.example: Above the treeline only grass survives.
items.exampleCN: 林木线以上只有草能存活。

items.meaning: the upper branches of a tree
items.example: Birds gathered in the treetop.

definition_zh: 巨大的；极大的；极好的；了不起的
definition_en: extremely great in size, amount, or effect, or extremely good
core_image: 一面山壁横在眼前，仰头看到脖颈发酸才见顶
scene: 站在峡谷边抬头，两壁高得让人后退半步，风从下面直往上冲。The canyon drops a tremendous distance to the river.
sceneCN: 这里 tremendous 是「巨大的」（第 1 个义项：体积、数量或影响极大）；句意为峡谷到河面的落差极大。仰头看不清顶的山壁正是这个词的画面。

pos.zh: 形容词：极好的；了不起的

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「极大地；非常」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「巨大」
同根名词，义为「震动；颤栗」

senses.title: Extremely great in size
senses.definition: very great in size, extent, or degree
senses.definitionCN: 在体积、范围或程度上非常大
senses.example: They crossed a tremendous desert.
senses.exampleCN: 他们穿过一片巨大的沙漠。
senses.why: A thing so great that one trembles at it is simply great in size, which is the direct descendant.
senses.whyCN: 大到让人发抖之物，直接就成了「体积巨大」，这是最直接的后代义。

senses.title: Extremely great in amount
senses.definition: very large in number or quantity
senses.definitionCN: 在数量上很大
senses.example: A tremendous number of people came.
senses.exampleCN: 来了极多的人。
senses.why: Number is only size counted, so the same adjective moves from space to quantity.
senses.whyCN: 数量不过是数出来的体积，所以同一个形容词从空间挪到数目上。

senses.title: Extremely strong in force
senses.definition: very strong in effect or force
senses.definitionCN: 在效力或影响上非常强
senses.example: The plan met tremendous opposition.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划遭到极大的反对。
senses.why: Force that makes people tremble is the sense closest to the Latin, applied to effect rather than body.
senses.whyCN: 让人发抖的力量最接近拉丁原义，只是作用在效果而非身体上。

senses.title: Extremely good
senses.definition: excellent or wonderful, in everyday approval
senses.definitionCN: 在日常赞许中表示「很棒」
senses.example: We had a tremendous time.
senses.exampleCN: 我们玩得非常开心。
senses.why: Weakened further, the awe becomes everyday praise for something excellent.
senses.whyCN: 再弱化一步，那份敬畏就变成对好东西的日常夸赞。

senses.title: Arousing awe or dread
senses.definition: so great as to cause wonder or fear, the oldest sense
senses.definitionCN: 大到令人惊叹或畏惧，这是最古老的义项
senses.example: The storm came on with tremendous force,
senses.exampleCN: 风暴以令人畏惧的力量袭来。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: tremendus names what must be trembled at.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：tremendus 指的就是「必须对它发抖」之物。

intro.en: The word is Latin tremendus, to be trembled at, from tremere, to tremble.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语 tremendus，意为「令人发抖的」，出自动词 tremere（发抖）。

items.en: Tremere means to tremble, and tremendus is the thing one must tremble at.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tremere 意为发抖，tremendus 就是「必须对它发抖」之物。

items.en: The Latin gerundive ending -ndus marks something that ought to be feared or done.
items.cn: 拉丁动形词词尾 -ndus 标记「应该被畏惧或应做」之物。

items.en: English first uses the word for things that inspire awe and dread.
items.cn: 英语最初用这个词指引起敬畏与恐惧的事物。

items.en: In the nineteenth century it weakens into a general word for very great.
items.cn: 十九世纪它弱化为泛指「非常大」的词。

items.en: Recent usage adds an everyday sense of very good.
items.cn: 近期用法又添上「非常好」的日常义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the trem- root of trembling, while the near-meaning group gathers other words for very large.
note.cn: 形近组共用 trem-（发抖）词根，近义组汇集表示极大的其他词。

entries.definition: to shake slightly
a slight shaking
shaking, or timid
to a very great degree
very large indeed
extremely large
extremely wide in area
as large as a giant statue

normalIntro.en: The word contains tremble, and it once meant something that made you tremble.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词里含着 tremble，它原先指让人发抖的东西。

normal.en: Tremere is to tremble, so tremendous means to be trembled at.
normal.cn: tremere 是发抖，所以 tremendous 就是「令人发抖的」。

normal.en: Over time the trembling became mere size, and the word now means very great.
normal.cn: 久而久之，那份颤抖只剩下「大」，如今意为极大。

normal.en: Tremor and tremulous share the same root, so they are one family.
normal.cn: tremor 与 tremulous 同根，属于一个家族。

normal.en: The adverb tremendously means to a great degree.
normal.cn: 副词 tremendously 意为「极大地」。

normal.en: In speech it also means very good, as in a tremendous day.
normal.cn: 口语里也表示很好，如 a tremendous day。

abstract.en: Picture a cliff so high that your neck aches to see the top.
abstract.cn: 想象一面山壁高到抬头看到脖子酸。

abstract.en: Feel the small tremble in your legs at the edge.
abstract.cn: 感受站在边沿时腿上的那阵轻颤。

abstract.en: Then let the same shake become praise for a good meal.
abstract.cn: 再让这阵颤动变成对一顿好饭的称赞。

examples.en: The project required a tremendous amount of work.
examples.cn: 这个项目需要大量的工作。

examples.en: She felt tremendous pressure before the exam.
examples.cn: 考试前她感到巨大的压力。

examples.en: You did a tremendous job on the report.
examples.cn: 这份报告你做得非常出色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「穿门得死」——门大得要穿过去都累死，真是巨大。

root: 拉丁语 tremere（发抖）的动形词 tremendus（令人发抖的）；同族有 tremble、tremor、tremulous

sensesIntro.en: All senses descend from awe: something so great that a person trembles at it.
sensesIntro.cn: 所有义项都源自敬畏：某物大到让人发抖。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cliff so high the neck aches.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面高到脖子发酸的山壁。

branches.en: The size and number senses, the plain modern use.
branches.cn: 体积与数量义：现代最普通的用法。

branches.en: The force sense, where the effect is overwhelming.
branches.cn: 力量义：影响压倒一切。

branches.en: The praise sense, borrowed from admiring talk.
branches.cn: 赞扬义：从赞赏的话里借来。

branches.en: The awe sense, the oldest and most literal.
branches.cn: 敬畏义：最古老也最字面。

branches.en: The cliff sense, the plain picture of size.
branches.cn: 峭壁义：体积最朴素的画面。

intro.en: The adjective is a Latin gerundive, a form that marks what ought to be feared or done.
intro.cn: 这个形容词是拉丁动形词，这种形式标记「应被畏惧或应做的事」。

latinIntro.en: The trem- stem gives tremble, tremor, tremulous, and tremendous.
latinIntro.cn: trem- 词干生出 tremble、tremor、tremulous 与 tremendous。

items.example: The stem gives tremor and tremble.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干生出 tremor 与 tremble。

items.example: Tremendus is the source of tremendous.
items.exampleCN: tremendus 是 tremendous 的来源。

items.example: Even the suffix -ous survives in tremendous.
items.exampleCN: 连 -ous 这个形容词词尾都留在 tremendous 里。

items.example: Her hands tremble in cold.
A tremor ran through the floor.
He gave a tremulous answer.

items.meaning: to be trembled at, hence huge
items.example: A tremendous wave hit the wall.
The film was tremendously popular.
The tremendousness of the task scared them.
items.exampleCN: 任务的巨大让他们害怕。

definition_zh: 趋势；倾向；潮流；走向
definition_en: a general direction in which something is developing or changing over time
core_image: 纸上一条折线慢慢向上爬，旁边标着几个年份
scene: 办公室里，分析师把几年的销量画成折线，线在最后一段明显上扬。The trend in sales has been upward for three years.
sceneCN: 这里 trend 是「趋势；走向」（第 1 个义项：事物随时间发展的总方向）；句意为销量的走势三年来一直在上升。纸上那条慢慢上扬的折线，就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 由 trend 加 -y 构成，义为「时髦的；赶潮流的」
由 trend 与 setter 复合，义为「引领潮流的人」
由 trend 加 -ing 构成，义为「正在流行的」

senses.title: The line on the graph
senses.definition: the general direction in which a situation is moving over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 情况在一段时间内发展的总方向
senses.example: The trend in sales has been upward for three years.
senses.exampleCN: 销量的走势三年来一直在上升。
senses.why: The word began as a turning of a river or a coast, and a line that keeps turning one way became a trend.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指河流或海岸的转弯，而一直朝一边转的线就成了趋势。

senses.title: What everyone is doing
senses.definition: a fashion or habit that many people take up at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 许多人同时接受的时髦做法
senses.example: Short jackets are the trend this autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 短外套是今年秋天的潮流。
senses.why: When many people turn the same way at once, the direction looks like a fashion to follow.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人同时转向同一个方向，这个方向看起来就像可以追随的风尚。

senses.title: Leaning in one direction
senses.definition: to move or develop generally in a stated direction
senses.definitionCN: 大体朝某个方向移动或发展
senses.example: Prices trended downward through the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 整个夏天价格趋于下降。
senses.why: The verb keeps the oldest picture: a course that keeps bending the same way.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了最古老的画面：一条一直朝同一方向弯的走向。

senses.title: Turning away from a fashion
senses.definition: to move away from a popular style in a new direction
senses.definitionCN: 离开流行样式，转向新的方向
senses.example: Designers are turning away from bright colours this year.
senses.exampleCN: 设计师今年正逐渐远离鲜亮的颜色。
senses.why: The verb keeps the old idea of a course bending, and fashion courses bend too.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词保留着航线折弯的旧意，时尚的走向同样会折弯。

intro.en: Trend first named the turning of a coastline or a river, and only later the direction of a set of figures.
intro.cn: trend 最初指海岸线或河流的转弯，后来才指一组数字的方向。

items.en: The verb trendan meant to turn or revolve, close to the modern tr-, dr- turn family.
items.cn: 古英语动词 trendan 意为转动、旋转，与表示「转」的词族相近。

items.en: A trend was the curve of a shore or the bend of a river.
items.cn: 中古英语里 trend 指海岸的弧线或河流的弯处。

items.en: Sailors spoke of the trend of a coast as its general direction.
items.cn: 水手用 the trend of a coast 指海岸的大致走向。

items.en: Statistics borrowed the word for the general direction of changing numbers.
items.cn: 统计学借用这个词，指变化中的数字的总方向。

items.en: Twentieth-century magazines applied it to fashion, giving the sense of a popular style.
items.cn: 二十世纪的杂志把它用在时尚上，产生了流行风潮的含义。

note.en: The first group shares the trend stem, the second holds other words for direction and fashion.
note.cn: 第一组共享 trend 词干，第二组收其他表示方向与流行的词。

entries.definition: Very fashionable.
Currently popular online.
A person who starts a fashion.
A leaning toward a kind of behaviour.
A popular style at a given time.
The line along which something moves.

normalIntro.en: Trend is a short word for a long line: the way things have been going and are likely to keep going.
normalIntro.cn: trend 是个短词，说的是长线：事情一路走来的方向，以及大概会继续走下去的方向。

normal.en: The verb is the same word: prices trend up.
normal.cn: 动词形式一模一样：prices trend up。

normal.en: The adjective trendy cuts the d and adds y.
normal.cn: 形容词 trendy 去掉 d 再加 y。

normal.en: A trendsetter sets the trend for others to follow.
normal.cn: trendsetter 设下潮流让旁人跟随。

normal.en: The plural is simply trends.
normal.cn: 复数直接加 s：trends。

normal.en: Statistics made the word famous: a trend line on a chart.
normal.cn: 统计学让这个词流行：图表上的一条趋势线。

abstract.en: A coastline bending the same way for miles.
abstract.cn: 海岸线绵延数里朝同一方向弯。

abstract.en: Water finding one slope and staying with it.
abstract.cn: 水找到一面斜坡，就一路顺着它。

abstract.en: Many people turning their heads at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 许多人同时把头转向同一个方向。

examples.en: There is a clear trend toward smaller cars in the city.
examples.cn: 这座城市明显有偏爱小车的趋势。

examples.en: Rents in the old quarter have trended upward since spring.
examples.cn: 老城区的租金自春天以来趋于上涨。

examples.en: She never follows the fashion of the season.
examples.cn: 她从不追随当季的风尚。

dict_mnemonic.text: trend 里的 tren 一念就像「转」——大家往一个方向转，就成了潮流。

root: 古英语 trendan（转动），中古英语指海岸或河流的弯向，近代经统计学与时尚用语扩展为「趋势、潮流」；同族词有 trendy、trendsetter、trending。

sensesIntro.en: First the direction of a changing figure, then the fashion many follow, then the verb for moving that way.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是变化数字的方向，再是众人追随的时髦，最后是朝那个方向走的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bending line on a chart.
core.cn: 核心意象：图表上弯曲的线。

branches.en: The figure branch: numbers moving one way.
branches.cn: 数字分支：数字朝一个方向走。

branches.en: The fashion branch: many people turning together.
branches.cn: 时尚分支：许多人一起转向。

branches.en: The action branch: a course leaning one way.
branches.cn: 动作分支：走势朝一边倾。

branches.en: The chart branch: both are read on a line.
branches.cn: 图表分支：两者都在一条线上读出。

branches.en: The crowd branch: a habit becomes a general direction.
branches.cn: 人群分支：一种习惯变成总方向。

intro.en: Trend is a short Germanic stem that now builds compounds and derivatives in business and fashion.
intro.cn: trend 是短小的日耳曼语词干，如今在商业与时尚领域构成复合词与派生词。

latinIntro.en: The stem is not Latin; the Latin words below are cousins through shared Indo-European roots.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干并非拉丁语；下面的拉丁词只是通过共同印欧词根构成的远亲。

items.example: The stem works as noun and verb alike.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干既可作名词也可作动词。

items.example: It forms trendy, full of fashion.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 trendy，满身时尚的。

items.example: It forms trending, popular right now.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 trending，眼下正走红的。

items.example: The two words say what the person does.
items.exampleCN: 两个词直接说出这个人做的事。

items.example: Up names the direction of the line.
Down names the opposite direction.
The line makes the direction visible.
Several trends appeared at once.

definition_zh: 试验；试用；审判；审讯
definition_en: a test of something to see whether it works, or the formal hearing of a case in a court
core_image: 一辆贴着彩条的车在试验场上绕圈，工程师盯着屏幕记数据
scene: 试验场上有一辆涂着彩条的车，工程师坐在场边的帐篷里看屏幕。The new engine is still on trial before it goes on sale.
sceneCN: 这里 trial 是「试验；试用」（第 1 个义项：为检验效果而进行的测试）；句意为这款新发动机在上市前仍在试用测试中。贴着彩条在场上绕圈的车，就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: trial 的词根，义为「尝试；审判」
由 try 与 out 复合，义为「选拔；试用」
由 try 加 -ing 构成，义为「令人恼火的；艰难的」

senses.title: The test run
senses.definition: an act of testing something over a period to see how well it works
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间内测试某物效果如何的行为
senses.example: The new engine is still on trial before it goes on sale.
senses.exampleCN: 这款新发动机在上市前仍在试用测试中。
senses.why: The ending -al turns the verb try into a noun, and the oldest sense is the testing of something.
senses.whyCN: -al 后缀把动词 try 变为名词，最古老的含义就是检验某物。

senses.title: The day in court
senses.definition: the formal examination of a case by a judge and often a jury
senses.definitionCN: 由法官及常设陪审团对案件进行的正式审理
senses.example: The trial lasted three weeks and ended with a verdict.
senses.exampleCN: 这场审判持续了三周，以裁决结束。
senses.why: A court also tests the facts of a case, so the legal hearing borrowed the same word as the engine test.
senses.whyCN: 法庭同样在检验案件的事实，于是庭审与发动机测试共用了同一个词。

senses.title: A hard testing time
senses.definition: a person or situation that tests your patience or strength
senses.definitionCN: 考验人耐心或承受力的人或处境
senses.example: Looking after three children alone was a real trial.
senses.exampleCN: 独自照料三个孩子真是一场考验。
senses.why: Anything that puts you under pressure is testing you, so hard days wear the same label.
senses.whyCN: 任何给你压力的事都在检验你，于是艰难的日子也挂上同一种标签。

senses.title: The person who is tested
senses.definition: a person taking part in a test to be chosen for a team or a job
senses.definitionCN: 参加测试以争取进入队伍或获得职位的人
senses.example: Three new players were on trial with the club in July.
senses.exampleCN: 七月有三名新球员在俱乐部试训。
senses.why: The noun can name a thing tested or a person tested, because both stand in front of a judge.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词既能指被检验的物，也能指被检验的人，因为两者都站在评判者面前。

intro.en: Trial is a noun made in English from the French verb trier, to sift or pick out, and it names whatever has been tested.
intro.cn: trial 是英语用来自法语动词 trier（筛、挑）造出的名词，指被检验过的东西。

items.en: Trier meant to sift grain or to sort things by quality.
items.cn: trier 意为筛谷物或按品质分类。

items.en: Tribulare and tritare lie behind French trier, all about rubbing or sorting.
items.cn: 法语 trier 的背后是 tribulare 与 tritare，都涉及摩擦或分选。

items.en: English formed trial on the French stem, first for the testing of metal and goods.
items.cn: 英语在法语词干上造出 trial，最初指检验金属与货物。

items.en: Law courts adopted the word for the hearing that tests a case.
items.cn: 法院借这个词指检验案情的庭审。

items.en: Everyday speech extended it to anything that tests a person.
items.cn: 日常语言把它扩展到任何考验人的事情。

note.en: The first group shows the try family, the second holds other words for tests and hearings.
note.cn: 第一组是 try 词族，第二组是其他表示测试与审理的词。

entries.definition: To make an attempt or test something.
Annoying and hard to bear.
A test to choose players or workers.
A check of quality or ability.
A session in which a case is examined.
A controlled attempt to find out something.

normalIntro.en: Trial is try with a thin -al added: what you get when you try something over and over.
normalIntro.cn: trial 就是 try 加一个轻薄的 -al：反复尝试之后得到的那件事。

normal.en: The y of try becomes i before the suffix: trial.
normal.cn: try 的 y 在词尾前变成 i：trial。

normal.en: Stand trial means you are being tested in court.
normal.cn: stand trial 意为在法庭上受检验。

normal.en: A trial period is time given to see if something works.
normal.cn: trial period 是检验一段时间看是否可行的期限。

normal.en: The plural only adds s: trials.
normal.cn: 复数只加 s：trials。

normal.en: A clinical trial tests a medicine on people.
normal.cn: clinical trial 是在人身上检验药物。

abstract.en: A marker line painted on a test track.
abstract.cn: 试验跑道上画的一条标线。

abstract.en: A small sample of cloth pulled between finger and thumb.
abstract.cn: 指尖搓过的一小块布样。

abstract.en: A long day that keeps asking how much you can carry.
abstract.cn: 漫长的一天，不断问你能承住多少。

examples.en: The drug is being tested in a large clinical trial.
examples.cn: 这种药正在一项大型临床试验中检验。

examples.en: She is standing trial for the theft of two paintings.
examples.cn: 她因盗窃两幅画而受审。

examples.en: The first month is a trial period without any cost.
examples.cn: 第一个月是免付费试用期。

dict_mnemonic.text: trial 里有 try——凡 trial 就是 try 出来的东西。

root: 由法语动词 trier（筛、挑）的词干加 -al 构成，源自中世纪拉丁语 tribulare、tritare，本义与筛选、摩擦有关；同族词有 try、trying、tryout。

sensesIntro.en: First the test of an object, then the test of a case in court, then any hard test of a person.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是检验物件，再是法庭上检验案情，最后是任何对人的艰难考验。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a marked track and a ticking screen.
core.cn: 核心意象：画着标线的跑道与跳动的屏幕。

branches.en: The product branch: a thing tested before sale.
branches.cn: 产品分支：上市前被检验的东西。

branches.en: The court branch: a case tested by a judge.
branches.cn: 法庭分支：由法官检验的案件。

branches.en: The person branch: a day that tests you.
branches.cn: 人分支：考验你的一天。

branches.en: The testing branch: both asks whether it holds.
branches.cn: 检验分支：两者都在问它是否站得住。

branches.en: The strain branch: weighing a person or a fact.
branches.cn: 承重分支：称量一个人或一项事实。

intro.en: Trial is formed from the French verb stem tri plus the noun suffix -al, a pattern English still uses freely.
intro.cn: trial 由法语动词词干 tri 加名词后缀 -al 构成，这一构词法英语至今仍常用。

latinIntro.en: Latin tritare, to rub or grind, is behind the French stem, and the words below show the same origin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tritare（磨、擦）是法语词干的前身，下面的词显示同一来源。

items.example: The stem carries the act of sorting for quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干承载按品质分选的行动。

items.example: It turns trying into a trial.
items.exampleCN: 它把尝试变成一次试验。

items.example: The verb names the bare action.
The participle became an adjective of strain.
items.exampleCN: 分词变成了表示煎熬的形容词。

items.example: The noun names what was tried.
items.exampleCN: 名词指被试验的那件事。

items.example: Several trials produced the same answer.
items.exampleCN: 几次试验得出同样的答案。

items.meaning: a public test for a place
items.example: Out marks a full attempt to the end.
items.exampleCN: out 标记把事情试到底。

items.example: Re adds another attempt after a failure.
items.exampleCN: re 表示失败后再来一次。

definition_zh: 诡计；把戏；窍门；戏弄；哄骗
definition_en: a clever act meant to deceive or amuse someone, or to deceive a person in that way
core_image: 一只手把硬币从这个人眼前晃过，却从那人耳后取出
scene: 街头围了一圈人，那个戴帽子的男人把手绢一晃，鸽子从袖口飞了出来。He knows a trick that makes a coin disappear.
sceneCN: 这里 trick 是「戏法、把戏」（第 2 个义项：逗人一乐的巧妙手法）；句意为他会一个让硬币消失的戏法。手一晃、东西换个地方出现，正是这个词的核心画面。

derivatives.zh: 名词加 -y 构成形容词，义为「棘手的；狡猾的」
名词加 -ery 构成，义为「欺骗行径」
名词加 -ster 构成，义为「骗子；恶作剧者」

senses.title: A plan to deceive someone
senses.definition: a clever but dishonest plan to get something from someone
senses.definitionCN: 巧妙却不老实、想从别人那里得利的计谋
senses.example: It was a trick to make him sign the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个骗他签字的诡计。
senses.why: The word comes from Old French trickier, to deceive, and its oldest sense is a cheat or a deceit.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自古法语 trickier（欺骗），最早的义项就是骗人或骗术。

senses.title: A clever act that amuses
senses.definition: a skilful performance, such as a card trick, done to entertain
senses.definitionCN: 为逗乐而做的熟练表演，如纸牌戏法
senses.example: The children loved the card trick.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们很喜欢那个纸牌戏法。
senses.why: A cheat and a magic show differ only in intent: both turn on a hidden method.
senses.whyCN: 骗人的手法与魔术表演只差用心：两者都靠一套藏着的方法。

senses.title: A clever way of doing something
senses.definition: a special way of doing a task that makes it easier
senses.definitionCN: 让事情变容易的特殊做法
senses.example: The trick is to stir the sauce slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 窍门是慢慢地搅酱汁。
senses.why: The hidden method that deceived someone can also simply help: then we call it the trick.
senses.whyCN: 那套藏着的方法如果不为骗人而是帮忙，我们就叫它窍门。

senses.title: To deceive someone
senses.definition: to make someone believe something untrue so that you gain an advantage
senses.definitionCN: 让人相信不实之事以取得好处
senses.example: They tricked him out of his savings.
senses.exampleCN: 他们骗走了他的存款。
senses.why: The verb is the act behind the noun: to work the hidden method on a person.
senses.whyCN: 动词是名词背后的动作：把藏着的方法用在某个人身上。

senses.title: A habit or mannerism
senses.definition: a peculiar habit of speech or behaviour that a person is known for
senses.definitionCN: 某人为人熟知的言语或举止习惯
senses.example: He has a trick of raising one eyebrow.
senses.exampleCN: 他有个挑一挑眉的习惯。
senses.why: A repeated piece of behaviour becomes as automatic as a practised sleight.
senses.whyCN: 反复出现的小动作，会像练熟的手法一样成为本能。

intro.en: The word comes from Old French trique, a deceit or a cheat, and the verb trickier, to deceive.
intro.cn: 这个词来自古法语 trique（欺骗、诈术）与动词 trickier（欺骗）。

items.en: Trique means a deceit, a shift, or a cheating play, and is used of dice and dealings.
items.cn: 古法语 trique 意为诈术、花招、骗人的把戏，用于骰子与交易。

items.en: English borrows the noun in the fifteenth century for a deceitful act.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个名词，指欺诈行为。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the word covers harmless sleight of hand and card play.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个词已涵盖无害的手法与纸牌戏法。

items.en: Later it names the clever knack of a trade and the odd habit of a person.
items.cn: 后来又用来指行业的技巧与一个人的怪癖。

items.en: The ultimate origin is uncertain; the word may be related to Old French trichier, to cheat.
items.cn: 最终来源不确定；可能和古法语 trichier（欺骗）有关。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words differing by one letter or sharing the stem, while the near-meaning group names other deceptions and knacks.
note.cn: 形近组汇集只差一个字母或共用词干的短词，近义组列出其他骗术与诀窍。

entries.definition: difficult or requiring care
the use of tricks to deceive
a large road vehicle
to flow in a thin slow stream
a playful trick on someone
to make someone believe what is false
a special skill at doing something
a false appearance made by a performer

normalIntro.en: Five letters, one sharp sound, and a family that grows from it.
normalIntro.cn: 五个字母，一个短促的音，还长出一整个词族。

normal.en: Tricky adds -y and means full of tricks, so difficult.
normal.cn: tricky 加 -y，意为满是机关，所以是棘手。

normal.en: Trickery adds -ery and names the practice of deceiving.
normal.cn: trickery 加 -ery，指欺骗的行径。

normal.en: A trickster is the person who plays the tricks.
normal.cn: trickster 就是耍弄这些把戏的人。

normal.en: Do the trick means the method works, with no deceit at all.
normal.cn: do the trick 指办法奏效，毫无欺骗之意。

normal.en: The verb takes a direct object and usually into: trick him into signing.
normal.cn: 这个动词带宾语，常加 into：trick him into signing。

abstract.en: Picture a coin leaving one palm and appearing behind an ear.
abstract.cn: 想象硬币离开一只手心，却出现在耳后。

abstract.en: Watch the empty palm open flat to prove nothing is there.
abstract.cn: 看那只空手摊平，证明什么也没有。

abstract.en: Then put that same sleight into a recipe and call it the trick.
abstract.cn: 再把这套手法放进菜谱里，就叫做窍门。

examples.en: The old trick of hiding a key under a flowerpot failed.
examples.cn: 把钥匙藏在花盆下这个老花招不管用了。

examples.en: It took me a while to learn the trick of folding the dough.
examples.cn: 我花了好一阵才学会折面团的窍门。

examples.en: They tricked the old man into paying twice.
examples.cn: 他们骗那位老人付了两次钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「踹克」——一脚踹开攻克对手的诡计，全靠手法。

root: 古法语 trique（诈术）与动词 trickier（欺骗），十五世纪进入英语；同族有 tricky、trickery、trickster，最终来源不确定

sensesIntro.en: One hidden method runs through every sense: it may cheat, amuse, help, or simply become a habit.
sensesIntro.cn: 一套藏着的方法贯穿所有义项：它可以骗人、逗乐、帮忙，或干脆变成一个习惯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coin that leaves one palm and appears elsewhere.
core.cn: 核心意象：硬币离开一只手心，在别处出现。

branches.en: The deceitful sense, where the method is used against someone.
branches.cn: 欺骗义：那套方法被用来对付人。

branches.en: The performing sense, where the method only entertains.
branches.cn: 表演义：那套方法只为逗乐。

branches.en: The helpful sense, where the same method makes work easy.
branches.cn: 助人义：同一套方法让活变简单。

branches.en: The verb sense, where the method is set in motion.
branches.cn: 动词义：把那套方法使出来。

branches.en: The habitual sense, where a mannerism repeats like a practised move.
branches.cn: 习惯义：小动作像练熟的手法一样重复。

intro.en: The word is short, but it builds a family with three productive suffixes.
intro.cn: 这个词很短，却靠三个能产的词尾长出一族词。

latinIntro.en: The French source has no Latin relatives in English, so the Latin list here stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 它的法语来源在英语里没有拉丁亲族，所以这里的拉丁同源词留空。

items.example: He played a trick on us.
A tricky question caught everyone.
items.exampleCN: 一道棘手的题难住了所有人。

items.example: The deal was pure trickery.
The trickster fooled the whole village.
The path runs trickily downhill.
items.exampleCN: 这条小路刁钻地往山下走。

items.example: He underestimated the trickiness of the task.
items.exampleCN: 他低估了这件事的棘手程度。

items.meaning: a question designed to catch you
items.example: That was a trick question.
The children shouted trick or treat.
items.exampleCN: 孩子们喊着不给糖就捣蛋。

items.example: The move looked tricky, even trickish.
items.exampleCN: 这一步看着就刁，甚至有点诡。

definition_zh: 棘手的；难对付的；狡猾的；诡计多端的
definition_en: something difficult to deal with and needing care or skill, or a person who deceives by tricks
core_image: 脚下一块湿滑的石头：看起来普通，踩上去才知道要格外小心
scene: 登山路上向导停下来指着前方提醒大家放慢脚步。The guide stopped and said the next section of the path was tricky.
sceneCN: 这里 tricky 是「棘手的；难对付的」（第 1 个义项：难处理、需要小心的）；句意为向导提醒大家下一段路不好走。脚下那块湿滑的石头，就是这个词的画面。

pos.zh: 棘手的；难对付的；需要小心的

collocations.zh: 敏感地带；容易出问题的话题

derivatives.zh: 由 tricky 加 -ly 构成，义为「狡猾地；靠花招地」
由 tricky 加 -ness 构成，义为「棘手；狡猾」

senses.title: Difficult to deal with
senses.definition: hard to handle or deal with, and needing care or skill
senses.definitionCN: 难以处理，需要小心或技巧的
senses.example: The guide stopped and said the next section of the path was tricky.
senses.exampleCN: 向导停下来，说下一段路不好走。
senses.why: A trick is a move that surprises you, so a tricky thing behaves in ways you did not expect and must be handled carefully.
senses.whyCN: trick 是让人措手不及的花招，所以棘手的事会以意想不到的方式给你出难题，必须小心应付。

senses.title: Likely to catch you out
senses.titleCN: 暗藏陷阱的；容易出错的
senses.definition: likely to deceive people or make them make mistakes
senses.definitionCN: 容易让人上当或出错的
senses.example: The second question was tricky because it looked simpler than it was.
senses.exampleCN: 第二道题很刁钻，因为看起来比实际简单。
senses.why: When a test sets tricks for you, the question itself becomes a trap, so tricky describes anything designed to catch you out.
senses.whyCN: 当题目里设了圈套，题目本身就成了陷阱，所以 tricky 形容一切暗藏机关、引人出错的东西。

senses.title: Clever at deceiving
senses.definition: clever at deceiving people or getting what one wants by tricks
senses.definitionCN: 善于欺骗他人或用花招达到目的的
senses.example: Everyone knew he was a tricky trader who hid the real price.
senses.exampleCN: 大家都知道他是个滑头商人，总把真实价格藏着掖着。
senses.why: A person full of tricks uses them on others, so the word moves from things to people who cannot be trusted.
senses.whyCN: 满脑子花招的人会把花招用在别人身上，于是这个词从「事情」转到「不可信的人」。

intro.en: Tricky is built directly on the noun trick, adding the adjective suffix -y to describe whatever involves tricks.
intro.cn: tricky 直接由名词 trick 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，形容一切与花招相关的性质。

items.en: The noun trick came from Old French trique, linked to triquier meaning to cheat or trick, generally thought to trace further back to the Vulgar Latin verb triccare.
items.cn: 名词 trick 来自古法语 trique，与动词 triquier（欺骗）相关，一般认为可再追溯到通俗拉丁语动词 triccare。

items.en: The reconstructed verb triccare is usually explained as meaning to trick or cheat, though its deeper origin remains uncertain.
items.cn: 重构形式 triccare 一般解释为「耍花招、欺骗」，其更深的来源并不确定。

items.en: Trick entered English in the fifteenth century, first meaning a fraud or a cheating act, later widened to any clever or playful move.
items.cn: trick 于十五世纪进入英语，最初指欺诈行为，后来扩大到任何机巧或玩笑式的动作。

items.en: The adjective tricky appeared in the eighteenth century, first describing deceitful people, then spreading to difficult tasks and situations.
items.cn: 形容词 tricky 出现于十八世纪，最初形容狡猾的人，后来扩展到困难的任务与局面。

items.en: In modern usage tricky most often means difficult to deal with, while the older sense of deceitful survives chiefly in informal speech.
items.cn: 现代用法中 tricky 多指「难对付的」，「狡猾的」旧义主要保留在口语里。

note.en: Words that look or sound close to tricky, and words that sit near it in meaning.
note.cn: 与 tricky 形近或音近的词，以及与它意思相近的词。

entries.definition: A clever act intended to deceive or amuse.
entries.definitionCN: 为欺骗或逗乐而使的花招；诀窍

entries.definition: To flow slowly in a thin stream.
entries.definitionCN: 细流；滴淌。只是拼写相近，词源与花招无关

entries.definition: Informal word for slightly itchy or ticklish.
entries.definitionCN: 发痒的（口语）。只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: Hard to do, understand, or deal with.
entries.definitionCN: 困难的；难做的。中性词，不强调暗藏圈套

entries.definition: Needing careful handling because things can easily go wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 微妙的；需要谨慎对待的。强调容易伤及各方，而非耍花招

entries.definition: Clever at deceiving people to get what one wants.
entries.definitionCN: 狡猾的；善于骗人的。强调聪明的欺骗，不带「难办」义

normalIntro.en: Five anchors built on the noun trick and its family.
normalIntro.cn: 围绕名词 trick 及其词族的五条记忆锚点。

normal.en: tricky = trick + y, so anything full of tricks is tricky.
normal.cn: tricky＝trick（花招）＋ -y，满是花招的东西自然「棘手」。

normal.en: a tricky question is a question that hides a trick.
normal.cn: a tricky question 就是暗藏花招、让人上当的题目。

normal.en: a tricky path makes you watch every step, like a path full of hidden tricks.
normal.cn: a tricky path 像布满暗算的路，每一步都得留神。

normal.en: a tricky customer plays tricks on you in business.
normal.cn: a tricky customer 做生意时专给人使绊子、耍滑头。

normal.en: trick (n.) is the base word; tricky, trickily and trickiness all grow from it.
normal.cn: trick 是词根，tricky、trickily、trickiness 都由它派生。

abstract.en: A wet stone on a mountain path: it looks ordinary until you step on it.
abstract.cn: 山路上一块湿滑的石头：看起来普通，踩上去才知道厉害。

abstract.en: A gift box that looks plain but springs a toy out when opened.
abstract.cn: 一个看似普通的礼盒，一打开就弹出一个玩具吓人一跳。

abstract.en: Walking an icy sidewalk: every step is calm, careful, and slightly dangerous.
abstract.cn: 走在结冰的人行道上：每一步都稳、小心，且暗藏危险。

examples.en: Parking in this narrow street is really tricky for beginners.
examples.cn: 在这条窄街停车对新手来说真的很棘手。

examples.en: The reporter asked a tricky question that the minister tried to dodge.
examples.cn: 记者提了一个刁钻的问题，部长试图回避。

examples.en: He can be a bit tricky in negotiations, so read every clause.
examples.cn: 他在谈判中有时不太老实，所以每个条款都要细读。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「垂克一」——垂着一根看不见的克线，走一步都被它「克」一下，路自然难走；此为谐音联想，不是词源。

root: 一般认为来自名词 trick（花招；欺骗），加形容词后缀 -y 构成「满是花招的」；trick 的更早来源为古法语 trique，与通俗拉丁语 triccare（耍花招）相关，深源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: The core image is a hidden trick that catches you, and the senses move from hard situations to traps and then to deceitful people.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心意象是「暗藏的圈套让你吃亏」：先指难办的局面，再指设了陷阱的题目，最后落到耍花招的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hidden trick waiting to catch you off guard
core.cn: 核心意象：一个藏在暗处、专门让你措手不及的花招

branches.en: Anything that behaves unexpectedly becomes hard to handle.
branches.cn: 凡是出人意料的东西都变得难对付。

branches.en: When the trick is set deliberately, the task turns into a trap.
branches.cn: 当花招是故意设下的，任务就变成了陷阱。

branches.en: Traps and surprises both force you to slow down and take care.
branches.cn: 陷阱与意外都逼你放慢脚步、加倍小心。

branches.en: A person who lives by tricks earns the label of deceitful.
branches.cn: 靠花招吃饭的人就被贴上「狡猾」的标签。

branches.en: Once you have been caught out, you stop trusting tricky people and tricky ground.
branches.cn: 吃过一次亏后，就不再轻信狡猾的人与敏感的话题。

intro.en: Tricky is a simple adjective built on trick; the items below show the suffixes and relatives around it.
intro.cn: tricky 是由 trick 加后缀构成的简单形容词，以下条目展示它周边的后缀与同族词。

latinIntro.en: The family is usually traced to Vulgar Latin triccare, though the link is not fully certain.
latinIntro.cn: 这一族词一般认为可追溯到通俗拉丁语 triccare，但证据并不完全确定。

items.example: trick + y gives tricky, full of tricks.
items.exampleCN: trick 加 -y 得到 tricky，即「满是花招的」。

items.example: trickier, trickiest

items.meaningCN: 以某种方式（副词后缀，y 变 i）

trickiness, the quality of being tricky

items.meaning: a clever act meant to deceive or amuse

items.exampleCN: 你用那套老花招骗不了我。

items.meaning: the use of tricks to deceive
items.example: The deal was full of trickery.

items.meaning: a person who plays tricks on others
items.example: In old tales the trickster fox outwits everyone.
items.exampleCN: 在古老的故事里，狡猾的狐狸总是智胜所有人。

items.example: They tricked him into signing the paper.
items.exampleCN: 他们骗他签了那份文件。

definition_zh: 旅行；旅程；绊倒；（药物引起的）迷幻体验
definition_en: a journey to a place and back, especially a short one, or an act of catching your foot and stumbling
core_image: 一列小火车似的巴士沿山路开进雾里，车窗上映着笑脸
scene: 周末清晨，一群人背着包上了开往山里的巴士。We took a trip to the mountains and stayed for two nights.
sceneCN: 这里 trip 是「旅行；旅程」（第 1 个义项：去某地再回来的行程，尤指短途）；句意为我们去山里旅行，住了两晚。清晨背包装车的那群人，就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 由 trip 加 -er 构成，义为「（短途）游客」
由 trip 加 -ing 构成，义为「轻快的（步伐）」
以 tri-（三）构成，义为「三脚架」

senses.title: Out and back
senses.definition: a journey to a place, especially a short one that ends at home
senses.definitionCN: 到某地的一次行程，尤指以回家告终的短途
senses.example: We took a trip to the mountains and stayed for two nights.
senses.exampleCN: 我们去山里旅行了一趟，住了两晚。
senses.why: The word may come from an old verb for skipping, because a short journey is a lively hop out and back.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可能源自意为「轻跳」的旧动词，因为短途出行就是轻快地跳出再回来。

senses.title: The foot catches
senses.definition: to catch your foot on something and lose balance
senses.definitionCN: 脚被某物挡住而失去平衡
senses.example: He tripped over the edge of the carpet.
senses.exampleCN: 他被地毯的边角绊了一下。
senses.why: A hop that goes wrong becomes a stumble, and this literal sense still lives in the verb.
senses.whyCN: 跳得不好就成了踉跄，这一字面含义仍留在动词里。

senses.title: Setting something off
senses.definition: to cause a switch or a machine to start working
senses.definitionCN: 使开关或机器开始运作
senses.example: A loose wire tripped the alarm at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 一根松动的电线在半夜触发了警报。
senses.why: A light foot catches a lever, and the mechanism starts, so machines also get tripped.
senses.whyCN: 轻脚一碰钩住杠杆，机构便启动，于是机器也会被 trip。

senses.title: A single outbound turn
senses.definition: one leg of a journey, counted as a single unit
senses.definitionCN: 行程中的一段，按一个单位计数
senses.example: The truck made four trips between the quarry and the site.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车在采石场和工地之间跑了四趟。
senses.why: When journeys are counted, each single run out and back becomes one trip by itself.
senses.whyCN: 当行程被计数时，每一趟出去再回来本身就成了一次 trip。

intro.en: Trip is a short English word of uncertain origin, probably connected with old verbs for skipping and stumbling.
intro.cn: trip 是来源不确定的短小英语词，可能与表示跳跃与踉跄的旧动词有关。

items.en: No sure source is known; it appears in the Middle English period as a verb of light movement.
items.cn: 确切来源不明；它在中古英语时期已作为表示轻快动作的动词出现。

items.en: To trippen meant to step lightly, and also to stumble on a stone.
items.cn: trippen 意为轻步走，也指在石头上踉跄。

items.en: A short sea voyage was called a trip in the early modern period.
items.cn: 近代早期，一段短途海上航程被称作 a trip。

items.en: By the nineteenth century a trip covered any short journey by train or coach.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，trip 已指任何乘火车或马车的短途行程。

items.en: The machine sense, tripping a switch, grew out of the same light touch.
items.cn: 触发开关的机械义同样出自那次轻碰。

note.en: The first group shares the trip stem and sound, the second holds words for journeys and stumbles.
note.cn: 第一组共享 trip 的词干与读音，第二组收表示旅程与踉跄的词。

entries.definition: A person on a short trip.
Moving lightly or catching the foot.
Stumbled or set off a device.
Travel from one place to another.
A short pleasure trip with others.
To catch the foot and nearly fall.

normalIntro.en: Trip is a tiny word with two lives: a small hop out somewhere, and a small hop that goes wrong.
normalIntro.cn: trip 这个词很小，却有两重生活：轻快地跳出去一趟，以及轻跳失手的一下。

normal.en: Take a trip means go out and come back.
normal.cn: take a trip 意为出去再回来。

normal.en: Past forms double the p: tripped, tripping.
normal.cn: 过去式双写 p：tripped、tripping。

normal.en: Trip over is the everyday stumble phrase.
normal.cn: trip over 是日常的绊倒说法。

normal.en: The plural simply adds s: trips.
normal.cn: 复数直接加 s：trips。

normal.en: Tripper turns the word into a person.
normal.cn: tripper 把这个词变成一个人。

abstract.en: A duffel bag by the door on a Friday night.
abstract.cn: 周五晚上门口的一只行李包。

abstract.en: A stone on a path you did not look at.
abstract.cn: 路上你没留意的一块石头。

abstract.en: A light foot catching a wire and waking the alarm.
abstract.cn: 轻脚绊到一根线，把警报唤醒。

examples.en: The bus leaves before dawn for a day trip to the lake.
examples.cn: 去湖边一日游的大巴在天亮前出发。

examples.en: She tripped on the last stair and dropped her keys.
examples.cn: 她在最后一级台阶绊了一下，钥匙掉在地上。

examples.en: Our trip to the coast was cut short by the storm.
examples.cn: 我们的海边之行被暴风雨提前中断。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吹蒲」——吹着蒲公英去旅行；脚下一绊，就是 trip 的另一义。

root: 来源不确定（中古英语 trippen 意为轻步走、踉跄），近代扩展出「短途旅行」与「触发装置」两义；同族词有 tripper、tripping、tripped。

sensesIntro.en: First the short journey, then the stumble, then the small touch that sets a device going.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是短途旅行，再是踉跄，最后是那点轻碰把装置启动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bag by the door and a stone on the path.
core.cn: 核心意象：门口的行囊与路上的一块石头。

branches.en: The journey branch: a short way out and back.
branches.cn: 旅程分支：短程出去再回来。

branches.en: The body branch: a foot catching and slipping.
branches.cn: 身体分支：脚绊住并滑开。

branches.en: The mechanism branch: a light touch starts a machine.
branches.cn: 机械分支：轻轻一碰让机器启动。

branches.en: The hop branch: both grew from a light skip.
branches.cn: 跳跃分支：两者都出自轻跳。

branches.en: The trigger branch: feet and levers both catch.
branches.cn: 触发分支：脚与杠杆都会被钩住。

intro.en: Trip is a free stem of uncertain origin that easily takes endings such as -er and -ing.
intro.cn: trip 是来源不明的自由词干，可以方便地加上 -er、-ing 等词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the journey words below, which are cousins rather than direct ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的旅程词汇出自拉丁语，它们只是远亲而非直接祖先。

items.example: The stem also works as a verb.
It forms tripper, a short-trip visitor.
It forms tripping, moving lightly.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 tripping，轻快行进的。

items.example: Two trips in one month were too many.
items.exampleCN: 一个月两次旅行太多了。

items.example: The p doubles before the ending.
items.exampleCN: 加词尾前 p 要双写。

items.example: Day fixes the length of the outing.
items.exampleCN: day 限定了出游的长度。

items.example: Business names the reason for the journey.
The same letters open a word about three feet.
items.exampleCN: 同样的字母开头，构成了关于三只脚的词。

definition_zh: 部队；一群；成群结队地走；军队
definition_en: a group of soldiers, or a group of people or animals moving together
core_image: 一队人排着走，脚步一同落下，扬起一小片尘土
scene: 清晨的操场上，一排士兵沿着跑道走成一列，背囊轻轻晃动。The troop moved slowly along the ridge at dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 troop 是「部队、一队士兵」（第 1 个义项：成队行动的军人）；句意为部队在黎明时沿山脊缓缓行进。整齐同行的一队人正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 名词加 -er 构成，义为「骑兵；州警」
现在分词名词化，义为「列队行进」
合成词，义为「运兵车；运兵舰」

senses.title: A group of soldiers
senses.definition: a group of soldiers, especially a unit of cavalry or a body of troops in action
senses.definitionCN: 一队士兵，尤指骑兵单位或行动中的队伍
senses.example: The troop was ordered back to the base.
senses.exampleCN: 这支部队被命令返回基地。
senses.why: A troop is first a small body of riders, and the word keeps that picture of a band moving as one.
senses.whyCN: troop 最初指一小队骑手，这个词始终保留「一伙人走成一体」的画面。

senses.title: Soldiers in general
senses.definition: soldiers considered as a body, especially those sent to a place
senses.definitionCN: 作为整体的士兵，尤指派往某地的兵力
senses.example: Troops were sent to the border.
senses.exampleCN: 部队被派往边境。
senses.why: The plural widens the single unit into the whole body of soldiers on a front.
senses.whyCN: 复数把单个单位扩展成前线上的全部兵力。

senses.title: A group of people or animals
senses.definition: a group of people or animals moving together
senses.definitionCN: 一起行动的一群人或一群动物
senses.example: A troop of schoolchildren crossed the square.
senses.exampleCN: 一群小学生穿过广场。
senses.why: A band of soldiers is a band, and any other band moving together borrows the name.
senses.whyCN: 一队士兵本就是一伙人，其他成伙走动的也用这个名字。

senses.title: To move in a group
senses.definition: to walk somewhere in a group, often without much order
senses.definitionCN: 成群地往某处走，常显得杂乱
senses.example: The children trooped into the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们成群地涌进礼堂。
senses.why: The verb is the noun set in motion: a troop walking becomes to troop.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是让名词走起来：一队人走路就成了 troop。

senses.title: A cavalry unit in the army
senses.definition: a small mounted or armoured unit forming part of a squadron or battalion
senses.definitionCN: 骑兵或装甲部队里的小单位，属中队或营建制
senses.example: The troop formed up at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 这个骑兵连在门口集合。
senses.why: Military organisation keeps the oldest sense, a small body of riders.
senses.whyCN: 军队编制保留了最古老的义项：一小队骑手。

intro.en: The word comes from French troupe, a band or company, and is probably of Germanic origin.
intro.cn: 这个词来自法语 troupe（一伙、一队），大概源出日耳曼语。

items.en: Troupe means a band, a company, or a crowd, and is used of soldiers and of players.
items.cn: 法语 troupe 意为一伙、一队、一群人，既用于士兵也用于演员。

items.en: The French word probably goes back to a Germanic root meaning a crowd or a herd.
items.cn: 这个法语词可能追溯到日耳曼语里表示人群或畜群词根。

items.en: English borrows it in the sixteenth century for a body of soldiers.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入，指一队士兵。

items.en: The plural troops becomes the ordinary word for soldiers sent to a place.
items.cn: 其复数 troops 成了「派往某地的兵力」的通常说法。

items.en: The word also names a small cavalry unit and any group of animals or children.
items.cn: 这个词也指小型骑兵单位，以及任何一群动物或孩子。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the troupe spelling family, while the near-meaning group gathers other words for armed bodies and groups.
note.cn: 形近组同属 troupe 拼写家族，近义组汇集其他军队与群体的说法。

normalIntro.en: Troop and troupe are the same word split two ways: soldiers and players.
normalIntro.cn: troop 与 troupe 是同一个词的两条路：一边是兵，一边是演员。

normal.en: The plural troops is the everyday word for soldiers abroad.
normal.cn: 复数 troops 是「驻外部队」的日常说法。

normal.en: A trooper is the soldier in the troop.
normal.cn: trooper 就是队伍里的兵。

normal.en: Troupe keeps the French spelling for a company of actors.
normal.cn: troupe 保留法语拼法，指剧团。

normal.en: The verb usually goes with into or out of: they trooped out.
normal.cn: 动词常与 into 或 out of 连用：他们成群走出。

normal.en: A troop of monkeys works the same way as a troop of soldiers.
normal.cn: 一群猴子与一队士兵的用法相同。

abstract.en: Picture a line of soldiers walking a ridge at first light.
abstract.cn: 想象天刚亮时一列士兵走在山脊上。

abstract.en: Hear the boots land almost together.
abstract.cn: 听靴子几乎同时落地。

abstract.en: Then see a class of children do exactly the same on a stair.
abstract.cn: 再看一班孩子在同一段楼梯上做同样的动作。

examples.en: Fresh troops arrived at the front before winter.
examples.cn: 入冬前新部队抵达前线。

examples.en: A troop of monkeys crossed the road in single file.
examples.cn: 一群猴子排成一列过了马路。

examples.en: After the bell, the class trooped out into the yard.
examples.cn: 铃响后，全班成群涌到院子里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「出普」——一出营门就排成普普通通的一队人。

root: 法语 troupe（一伙、一队），可能源自日耳曼语「人群」词根，十六世纪进入英语；同族有 troupe、trooper

sensesIntro.en: Every sense names a body of beings moving together, from cavalry to schoolchildren.
sensesIntro.cn: 每个义项都指一起行动的一群，从骑兵到小学生。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: boots landing almost together along a ridge.
core.cn: 核心意象：靴子几乎同时落在山脊上。

branches.en: The soldier senses, where a small unit is meant.
branches.cn: 士兵义：指的是具体的小单位。

branches.en: The force sense, where the plural means all the soldiers there.
branches.cn: 兵力义：复数指当地全部士兵。

branches.en: The group sense, where children or animals form the band.
branches.cn: 群体义：孩子或动物组成这一伙。

branches.en: The verb sense, where the band starts walking.
branches.cn: 动词义：这一伙动起来了。

branches.en: The unit sense again, where the formation is what counts.
branches.cn: 再回单位义：关键在队形。

intro.en: The word is French in shape, and the family around it is small and concrete.
intro.cn: 这个词带法语形状，周围的词族小而具体。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin relative in English, so the Latin list here stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 它在英语里没有拉丁亲族，所以这里的拉丁同源词留空。

Troop gives troops.
Troop gives trooper.

items.meaning: a vehicle or ship for soldiers
items.example: The troop carrier left at dawn.

items.meaning: to walk out in a group
items.example: They trooped out of the hall.

items.meaning: the ceremony of marching the colours
items.example: Trooping the colour is held in June.
items.exampleCN: 军旗列队仪式在六月举行。

definition_zh: 麻烦；困难；烦扰；使烦恼；疾病
definition_en: a problem or difficulty, or the act of making someone worried or upset
core_image: 水面被搅得浑起来，鱼看不见，连倒影都碎了
scene: 深夜，修车师傅蹲在路边，车前盖敞开着，车主来回踱步打电话。The old car has given us a lot of trouble this year.
sceneCN: 这里 trouble 是「麻烦」（第 1 个义项：让人头疼的问题）；句意为这辆旧车今年给我们添了不少麻烦。搅浑的水面与来回踱步的画面正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 名词加 -some 构成形容词，义为「麻烦的；讨厌的」
过去分词形容词化，义为「困扰的；动荡的」
合成词，义为「惹麻烦的人」

senses.title: A problem or difficulty
senses.definition: a problem, difficulty, or unpleasant situation that must be dealt with
senses.definitionCN: 需要处理的难题、困难或令人不快的处境
senses.example: We had trouble finding the address.
senses.exampleCN: 我们找这个地址费了点劲。
senses.why: The verb behind the word means to stir up or disturb, and a stirred situation becomes a problem.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的动词意为搅动、扰乱，被搅乱的情形就成了麻烦。

senses.title: Worry or distress
senses.definition: a feeling of worry, anxiety, or unhappiness
senses.definitionCN: 担忧、焦虑或不快的情绪
senses.example: Her troubles seemed to lift after the call.
senses.exampleCN: 那通电话之后她的烦恼似乎散了。
senses.why: The stir that clouds the water also clouds the mind, so the word names inner unrest.
senses.whyCN: 搅浑水面的动荡同样会搅浑心里，所以这个词也指内心的不安。

senses.title: To cause someone worry
senses.definition: to make someone worried, annoyed, or uncomfortable
senses.definitionCN: 使某人担忧、不快或不安
senses.example: The noise troubled her all night.
senses.exampleCN: 那噪声扰了她一整夜。
senses.why: To trouble is to stir someone up, exactly as a stick stirs a pond.
senses.whyCN: trouble 就是把人搅动起来，正如一根棍子搅动池塘。

senses.title: Illness or a fault in a machine
senses.definition: an illness, or a fault in a machine or a part of the body
senses.definitionCN: 疾病，或机器、身体某部位出的毛病
senses.example: He has heart trouble and walks slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 他有心脏病，走路很慢。
senses.why: A body or an engine that is not running smoothly is in a disturbed state, so it has a trouble.
senses.whyCN: 身体或发动机运转不顺就是处于被扰动的状态，于是有了毛病。

senses.title: Extra effort taken to help
senses.definition: extra effort that one takes in order to do something for others
senses.definitionCN: 为他人做事而额外花的力气
senses.example: She took the trouble to write by hand.
senses.exampleCN: 她不嫌麻烦地手写了信。
senses.why: Stirring up effort on someone’s behalf is also a trouble, and the phrase keeps that effort visible.
senses.whyCN: 为别人搅起一番力气也是一种 trouble，这个短语把那份力气显出来。

intro.en: The word goes back through Old French to late Latin turbulare, to stir up, from turbare, to disturb.
intro.cn: 这个词经古法语回溯到晚期拉丁语 turbulare（搅动），源于 turbare（扰乱）。

items.en: Turba means a crowd, a tumult, or a disturbance, and turbare means to throw into confusion.
items.cn: 拉丁语 turba 意为人群、骚动、扰乱，动词 turbare 意为使混乱。

items.en: Turbulare, to stir up, is formed on turba and gives the later Romance words.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 turbulare（搅动）由 turba 构成，生出后来的罗曼语词。

items.en: Old French troubler means to disturb and also to make a liquid cloudy.
items.cn: 古法语 troubler 意为扰乱，也指把液体搅浑。

items.en: English borrows the noun and verb in the thirteenth century with both the literal and the mental sense.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入名词与动词，字面义与心理义一并带入。

items.en: Engineering and medicine give it the concrete senses of a fault and an illness.
items.cn: 工程与医学给了它「故障」与「疾病」两个具体义项。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Latin turb- family, while the near-meaning group names other problems and worries.
note.cn: 形近组汇集同出拉丁语 turb- 词族的词，近义组列出其他问题与烦恼的说法。
